name: Google Cloud Generative AI Leader
price: $99 plus tax (verify on the official page)
audience: Anyone who shapes gen AI adoption: business leaders, product and project managers, consultants, sales and technical staff. No hands-on technical experience required.
format: 50–60 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes, online-proctored or at a test centre, in English, Japanese or Spanish. Valid for 3 years. Results are pass/fail and Google does not publish the cut score; this site targets 720/1000 (about 69%) on its mocks, and you should aim for 85%+.
scenarios: Build or buy for a product team
verifyNotes: GAIL is a real Google Cloud certification. Confirm section names, weights, item count, duration, fee, languages, delivery (Kryterion) and validity against the official exam page and exam guide PDF. Google renames products often (Vertex AI -> Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agentspace -> Gemini Enterprise, Duet AI -> Gemini for Workspace): use current names and mention former names where learners will meet them. Never copy the official sample questions.

domains.name: Fundamentals of gen AI
skills: Explain AI, ML, deep learning, gen AI, foundation models and LLMs in plain language
Compare supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning and the ML lifecycle on Google Cloud
Judge data quality, structured vs unstructured and labelled vs unlabelled data
Describe the gen AI landscape layers (infrastructure, models, platforms, agents, applications)
Choose among Google models (Gemini, Gemma, Imagen, Veo) by modality, cost and latency
Identify business use cases where gen AI creates value

domains.name: Google Cloud’s gen AI offerings
skills: Explain why Google Cloud for gen AI: AI-optimized infrastructure (TPUs), openness, security
Position the Gemini app, Gems, Gemini Enterprise and Gemini for Google Workspace
Use customer experience offerings: Agent Search and the Customer Engagement Suite
Describe the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: Model Garden, agent building, tools, evaluation
Choose between low-code agent building and Google AI Studio

domains.name: Techniques to improve gen AI model output
skills: Name model limitations: hallucination, knowledge cutoff, bias, data dependency, edge cases
Apply Google-recommended mitigations: grounding, RAG, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, human in the loop
Use prompting techniques: zero-shot, few-shot, role, chain-of-thought, ReAct, prompt chaining
Explain grounding with Google Search, enterprise data and third-party data
Set sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k, output length) and safety settings
Monitor and evaluate models in production

domains.name: Business strategies for a successful gen AI solution
skills: Choose the right gen AI solution by need, skills, cost and control (buy, build, customise)
Integrate gen AI into an organisation: change management, sponsorship, skills
Measure impact with KPIs and ROI
Apply Google's Secure AI Framework (SAIF) and Google Cloud security tools
Apply responsible AI: fairness, privacy, transparency, accountability, explainability
